stories.headline: Florida judge throws out noncitizen-voting charge, saying only states set who can vote
stories.summary: U.S. District Judge David Leibowitz, a Biden appointee in South Florida, dismissed federal charges against Chelsea Cox, a Jamaican-born woman who voted in the 2020 presidential election without being a U.S. citizen. In a 31-page ruling he wrote that the Constitution gives the states, not Congress, the power to set voter qualifications, so the 1996 law that makes noncitizen voting in federal elections a crime is unconstitutional as applied to her. He rejected the Justice Department’s arguments from Congress’s power over immigration and from the Elections Clause. The ruling lands while the Trump administration is bringing noncitizen-voting cases and pressing states to check citizenship on the rolls.

stories.headline: DHS lawyer: third-country deportation or release — ‘Norway is not taking a rapist from Cuba’
stories.summary: Homeland Security general counsel James Percival told Fox News Digital that when a home country will not take someone back, the government has two choices: find another country, or release the person into the United States. “Norway is not taking a rapist from Cuba,” he said. The Supreme Court on Tuesday stayed a lower-court order that had restricted third-country removals, so the policy stays in effect while the justices hear the case in December. Percival said the tool is already written into the 1996 immigration statute and that earlier administrations mostly left it unused. This is his public defense of that authority, not a new court order.

stories.headline: FBI files: Crooks texted about 3D-printed parts and coded one-word messages before Butler
stories.summary: FBI records released to Judicial Watch show Thomas Matthew Crooks, who shot at President Trump in Butler on July 13, 2024, trading messages about a 3D printer more than a year earlier. On Feb. 9, 2023, an “unknown contact” asked, “Did you 3D print the parts?” From May 2023 through Jan. 3, 2024, Crooks sent a second contact strings of one- and two-word notes — “Hello red,” “Yolo,” and runs of letters — with the other side’s replies redacted. The same release includes a DHL notice for a package from Hong Kong and about 40 drone photos he took in February 2024, including shots of Pittsburgh stadiums.

stories.headline: Jack Smith’s deputy wrote he wanted the Speech or Debate Clause repealed
stories.summary: Newly surfaced 2021 messages show JP Cooney, who later became Jack Smith’s principal deputy, telling another prosecutor he was “an advocate for repealing” the Constitution’s Speech or Debate Clause, which shields members of Congress from prosecution over legislative acts. Senate Judiciary Chairman Chuck Grassley said Cooney and Smith later violated that protection by secretly obtaining toll records and text messages from dozens of members of Congress. Grassley called it what happens “when runaway Democrat government is in power.” Smith’s team led the federal cases into Trump’s challenge to the 2020 election and his handling of classified documents.

stories.headline: FlyDubai co-pilot named as Omani flyer barred in 2024 over extremist concerns
stories.summary: The co-pilot accused of attacking the captain of FlyDubai Flight 1073 with the cockpit crash axe has been identified as Hamam al-Hammami, 29, an Omani national, a Middle Eastern source told Fox News. Oman Air barred him from flying in 2024 over concerns about extremist views, and the source said he moved to Dubai later that year. The United Arab Emirates, which is leading the investigation, said the attack incapacitated Capt. Smit Machchhar and the jet plunged before people on board got control. A Gulf diplomat told the Associated Press that investigators are still asking whether he acted alone. The source said FlyDubai did not check with Oman Air before hiring him.

stories.headline: Man charged in Ann Widdecombe’s killing is now accused of plotting against Nigel Farage
stories.summary: British prosecutors on Friday charged Joshua Kerry, 28, of South Yorkshire, with preparing terrorist acts, including against Reform UK leader Nigel Farage. Kerry has been in custody since late July, accused of murdering former Reform and Conservative politician Ann Widdecombe. Prosecutors say he walked into her Devon home on July 8 while she was eating lunch, struck her in the head 21 times with a hammer, took her wallet, and left in about two minutes. The new charge covers conduct between May 31 and July 8. Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood called an attack on anyone in politics “an attack on us all.”

stories.headline: 128 Republicans ask HHS watchdog to review Planned Parenthood’s federal money
stories.summary: Rep. Chris Smith of New Jersey and Sen. James Lankford of Oklahoma led 128 Republican lawmakers in a letter asking Health and Human Services Inspector General T. March Bell to review Planned Parenthood Federation of America and its affiliates. They want the watchdog to look at money flowing through HHS programs, grants, contracts, and sub-awards and to say whether there is fraud, waste, abuse, or misrepresentation. If misconduct turns up, they ask for remedies that could include suspension, exclusion from federal health programs, or referrals to other authorities. The letter cites what the lawmakers call serious past allegations against the group and its affiliates.

stories.headline: France’s student riots widen: about 2,000 arrested as Paris blames the hard left
stories.summary: Riot police clashed with teenagers Friday in Strasbourg, Marseille, Rennes, and Paris as France’s student unrest escalated, Fox News reports, citing Reuters. Justice Minister Gérald Darmanin said about 2,000 people, most of them teenagers, have been arrested since the protests began, and roughly 400 high schools stayed closed. Education officials counted at least 65 school staff hurt, including 40 principals, about 170 injured students, and severe damage at more than 100 schools. The protests started over crowded classrooms, missing teachers, and hot buildings, and the government is increasingly blaming the hard left. Darmanin said parents should have to pay for property their children damage.

stories.headline: EPA: cyberattacks on U.S. water systems are up several-fold and aim to disrupt, not just ransom
stories.summary: EPA water chief Jess Kramer told Fox News Digital that cyberattacks on drinking-water and wastewater systems have risen “several fold,” and that the point is shifting from ransomware to knocking out service. “Everyday life completely crumbles” without that infrastructure, she said, from hospitals to daycares. Hackers have already hit computerized controls at more than 30 Minnesota water systems, forcing some utilities onto manual backups. Enforcement chief Jeff Hall said many systems are still running old equipment without basic protections such as changed passwords, and that system details are sometimes left online. The agency is warning utilities that a successful hit is a public-safety problem, not only a billing scam.

stories.headline: Tesla pushes Austin Robotaxi to 11 p.m.; Musk says night pets are the holdup
stories.summary: Tesla’s Robotaxi account said late Friday that unsupervised rides in Austin now run until 11 p.m., an hour past the 10 p.m. cutoff the service has used since Aug. 26, when the window was 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. seven days a week. Elon Musk quote-posted the note and said the limit on going later is animals that cameras struggle to see after dark: “Literally trying to avoid grey kittens on grey tarmac in the dark.” TeslaNorth notes the extra hour covers dinner and downtown events, and that the Austin fleet recently added its 67th Cybercab. Musk did not give a date for overnight service.

stories.headline: Musk confirms TSMC talks on the $16.8 billion Texas Terafab, with no deal yet
stories.summary: Elon Musk on Saturday confirmed that talks are underway with TSMC about a role in Terafab, the reported Tesla–SpaceX chip project in Grimes County, Texas, priced at an initial $16.8 billion. Replying to a post about the discussions, he wrote, “Just discussions, but something may come of it.” Columnist Tim Culpan reported Friday that the Taiwanese foundry may use Terafab as an anchor customer for a future Texas site. Intel was already described as a partner in April. The plant is meant to make chips for AI, robotics, and space, and Musk stopped short of announcing any agreement.

stories.headline: Side-by-side: unfolded iPhone Duo is about as wide as the iPhone 18 Pro Max is tall
stories.summary: A side-by-side video posted by @thetechchap, measured against Apple’s specs by 9to5Mac, shows the folding iPhone Duo’s open screen is the largest iPhone display yet, bigger than the iPhone 18 Pro Max. Lined up one way, the Duo’s 6.48-inch width is almost the same as the Pro Max’s 6.43-inch height. The Duo’s other side is 4.64 inches, against 3.07 inches for the Pro Max’s narrower edge, so the open phone is the roomier slab. Folded, it is the more pocketable of the two and easier to use in one hand.

stories.headline: Penguins open at home against Montreal, both clubs 1–0, with Dobes in the Canadiens net
stories.summary: Pittsburgh hosts Montreal on Saturday in the Penguins’ home opener, with both teams 1–0. The Penguins are 31–17–10 all-time in home openers. Montreal spoiled Gavin McKenna’s NHL debut with a 3–2 win over Toronto on Tuesday, and Jakub Dobes picked up his 37th career win in that game — only three Canadiens goalies have more wins through 60 games. Pittsburgh went 1–2 against Montreal last season, with two regulation losses before a shootout win in December. After tonight the schedule tightens: Winnipeg at home Monday, Washington on Friday, then a weekend back-to-back at Columbus and against Dallas.

stories.headline: Westport’s second town-wide tag sale is set for Oct. 17, with 22 homes already in
stories.summary: Westport is bringing back a town-wide tag sale on Saturday, Oct. 17, from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m., with Sunday, Oct. 18, as the rain date. Sales are at people’s houses, not one lot, and the Nolan Team at Compass builds the shopper map. Last spring more than 45 homes took part; 22 have signed up for this round, past the group’s goal of 20. Unsold items can be picked up afterward for the United Breast Cancer Foundation. No fresh free Trumbull item turned up beyond stories already in the archive, so this Fairfield County notice is the local stand-in.
